prompt:
A 68-year-old man was incidentally found to have an 8 mm right lung nodule on an abdominal CT. He underwent cholecystectomy 12 years ago. A follow-up noncontrast chest CT did not re-demonstrate the nodule, but instead showed multifocal bronchial wall thickening, tree-in-bud nodularity, and mucus plugging concerning for nontuberculous mycobacterial (NTM) infection. A Gram stain and routine sputum culture have been sent and are planning three induced sputum samples for AFB smear and mycobacterial culture. What empiric antibiotics or further testing (e.g., bronchoscopy) should be initiated?

Provide a comprehensive management plan including appropriate diagnostic workup, referrals, procedures if indicated, follow-up, and actions to avoid.

rubric_items.text: Defer empiric antimycobacterial therapy until adequate respiratory specimens establish a microbiologic diagnosis.
Assess whether compatible pulmonary symptoms, characteristic imaging, exclusion of alternative diagnoses, and accepted microbiologic criteria establish NTM pulmonary disease.
Obtain three induced sputum specimens on separate days for AFB smear and mycobacterial culture.
Review the pending routine sputum Gram stain and bacterial culture.
Obtain a detailed pulmonary symptom and relevant exposure history.
Review prior chest imaging to determine the chronicity and distribution of the airway abnormalities.
Refer the patient to pulmonology for evaluation of suspected NTM pulmonary disease and associated bronchiectatic airway changes.
Perform bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage for AFB testing if induced sputum cannot be obtained or remains nondiagnostic despite persistent suspicion.
Obtain species-level identification for every positive mycobacterial culture.
Obtain guideline-directed susceptibility testing for any clinically significant NTM isolate.
Order a respiratory Mycobacterium tuberculosis nucleic acid amplification test when tuberculosis remains in the differential diagnosis.
Order HIV antigen-antibody testing to assess for immunodeficiency.
Measure serum immunoglobulin levels to evaluate for humoral immunodeficiency.
Obtain a comprehensive metabolic panel with liver function tests as a baseline before potential multidrug therapy.
Obtain pulmonary function testing with spirometry, lung volumes, and diffusing capacity.
Initiate nebulized hypertonic saline for airway clearance when secretions are difficult to mobilize.
Provide an oscillating positive expiratory pressure device for airway clearance.
Arrange pulmonary follow-up within several weeks to review symptoms and available culture results, tailoring timing to clinical severity and culture availability.
Schedule repeat chest CT in approximately 6 months to assess the airway abnormalities for progression or resolution.
Counsel the patient that mycobacterial cultures commonly require 6 to 8 weeks for final results.
Advise prompt reassessment for hemoptysis, fever, weight loss, or worsening dyspnea.
Refer to infectious diseases for co-management if clinically significant NTM pulmonary disease is confirmed.
Obtain baseline visual acuity and color-vision testing before starting ethambutol.
Obtain a baseline electrocardiogram for QT assessment before starting macrolide-based therapy.
Reconcile medications for QT-prolonging interactions before starting macrolide-based therapy.
Start empiric azithromycin or other macrolide monotherapy for suspected NTM pulmonary disease.
Start an empiric macrolide-rifamycin-ethambutol regimen before microbiologic confirmation of NTM pulmonary disease.
Start empiric RIPE-type antituberculous therapy without evidence supporting active tuberculosis.

Start empiric antibacterial antibiotics solely for the CT airway abnormalities, without clinical evidence of acute bacterial pneumonia, a bacterial bronchiectasis exacerbation, or another bacterial infection warranting treatment.
Perform routine immediate bronchoscopy despite feasible planned induced sputum collection and no urgent independent indication.
Order PET-CT to evaluate the nodule that was not redemonstrated or the inflammatory airway findings.
Perform CT-guided biopsy of the previously reported 8 mm nodule that resolved on follow-up imaging.
Refer for wedge resection or VATS lung resection without a persistent target or microbiologic diagnosis.
Start inhaled amikacin empirically for the current unconfirmed NTM presentation.
Start systemic corticosteroids for the bronchial wall thickening, tree-in-bud nodularity, or mucus plugging.
Use an interferon-gamma release assay as the primary diagnostic test for NTM pulmonary disease.
Use serial routine bacterial sputum cultures as a substitute for AFB smear and mycobacterial culture.
Discontinue pulmonary follow-up solely because the initially reported nodule was not redemonstrated.
Start empiric antifungal therapy for the tree-in-bud abnormalities without evidence of fungal infection.
Institute strict airborne isolation solely because NTM pulmonary disease is suspected.
